title: Personal services income — Div 85 ITAA 1997
summary: Facet map: do the PSI rules apply? Spine: is it PSI (s 84-5 — mainly a reward for personal exertion) → employee/office holder/religious practitioner exception (s 85-35) → PSB gateway (any of the four Div 87 tests or a determination — exit via s 85-30 to the extent income is from a PSB) → Div 86 attribution for entity-derived PSI (s 86-15(1)-(5), with prompt-pay exception in s 86-15(4) and entity-PSB exception in s 86-15(3)) → employee-equivalence deduction limits (s 85-10 with the s 85-10(2) preserved categories). FACETS: results test 75% threshold (s 87-18), unrelated clients 2+ test (s 87-20), employment test (s 87-25), business premises test (s 87-30), entity deduction entitlements (s 86-60), associate super SG cap (s 85-25(3)). Subsection coverage: ss 84-5, 85-5, 85-10(1)-(2), 85-15, 85-20(1)-(3), 85-25(1)-(4), 85-30, 85-35(1)-(2), 86-15(1)-(5), 86-20, 86-25, 86-30, 86-60, 87-15, 87-18, 87-20, 87-25, 87-30 mapped; ss 86-75/86-80 determinations noted. Key ruling: TR 2022/3.

nodes.label: You earn income for personal work — do the PSI rules (Div 85/86) apply and limit your deductions?
nodes.body: Single question with facets. Spine: is it PSI → are you a PSB (exit) → entity attribution → employee-equivalence deduction limits. Facets carry the niche thresholds and where-to-look.

statute.title: Object of this Division

nodes.label: Is the income personal services income (s 84-5)?
nodes.body: PSI = income mainly a reward for your personal efforts or skills (the 'more than 50%' test). If the income rewards capital, equipment or others' work, Div 85/86 do not apply.

statute.title: What is personal services income

nodes.label: Not PSI — normal rules apply
nodes.body: If income is not mainly for personal exertion, it is business income under ordinary rules (s 6-5).

nodes.label: Are you an employee, office holder or religious practitioner (s 85-35)?
nodes.body: Div 85 does not apply to PSI received as an employee (s 85-35(1)(a)), office holder (s 85-35(1)(b) via Sch 1 TAA 1953 s 12-45(1)(a)-(e)), or religious practitioner (s 85-35(2) via s 12-47).

statute.title: Exception: employees, office holders and religious practitioners

nodes.label: Employee — normal employment deduction rules
nodes.body: Outside Div 85. Ordinary s 8-1 rules apply as an employee (TR 2020/1).

nodes.label: Do you conduct a personal services business (Div 86)?
nodes.body: If you pass any one of the four PSB tests — results (s 87-18), unrelated clients (s 87-20), employment (s 87-25), business premises (s 87-30) — or obtain a PSB determination (ss 86-75/86-80), you are a PSB. Under s 85-30, Div 85 does not apply to the amount/payment/contribution to the extent that it relates to income from you conducting a PSB. TR 2022/3 is the key ruling. Note: if 80% or more of PSI is from one source, only the results test applies (s 87-15(3)).

statute.title: What is a personal services business
Exception: personal services businesses

rulings.title: personal services income and personal services businesses

nodes.label: PSB — Div 85 does not apply (to the extent it relates to PSB income)
nodes.body: Income from conducting a PSB is treated as business income. s 85-30 disapplies Div 85 to the extent the amount relates to income from conducting a PSB. If the PSI is derived through an entity that conducts a PSB, s 86-15(3) also disapplies the attribution rules. Normal deduction rules apply.

nodes.label: Not a PSB — Div 85 deduction limits apply
nodes.body: You have PSI and are not a PSB. Div 85 limits deductions to employee-equivalent amounts: s 85-10(1) denies deductions for expenses an employee could not deduct, with preserved categories in s 85-10(2); s 85-15 limits home-office/room occupancy; s 85-20 limits associate payments; s 85-25 caps associate super deductions at the SG rate. If the PSI is earned through an entity, Div 86 attribution (s 86-15) and the entity deduction rule (s 86-60) also apply.

statute.title: Deductions for non-employees relating to personal services income
Deductions for amounts relating to a home office or room
Deductions for payments to associates
Deductions for superannuation for associates

nodes.label: Is the PSI derived through a personal services entity (company/trust/partnership)?
nodes.body: Div 86 attribution structure. s 86-15(1): the PSE's PSI is included in your assessable income. s 86-15(2): a PSE is a company/partnership/trust whose income includes your PSI. s 86-15(3): exception — this section does not apply if the amount is income from the entity conducting a PSB. s 86-15(4): exception — the amount is not attributed to you if the entity pays it to you as salary/wages within 14 days after the PAYG payment period. s 86-15(5): extent limitation — attribution only applies to amounts that would be assessable income of the entity. If attributed, your deduction entitlements follow Div 85 limits; the entity's deductions are limited under s 86-60.

statute.title: Effect of obtaining personal services income through a personal services entity
General rule for deduction entitlements of personal services entities

nodes.label: PSI derived directly by you (sole trader)
nodes.body: The Div 85 limits apply directly: s 85-10 (non-employee deductions), s 85-15 (residence occupancy), s 85-20 (associate payments), s 85-25 (associate super).

nodes.label: Entity's PSI attributed to you (Div 86)
nodes.body: The PSE's PSI is included in your assessable income under s 86-15(1), unless: (a) the entity conducts a PSB (s 86-15(3)), or (b) the entity pays the amount to you as salary/wages within 14 days (s 86-15(4)). Attribution is limited by s 86-15(5) to amounts that would be assessable income of the entity. If attributed, the entity deducts only what it could deduct as an individual per s 86-25 and must withhold per s 86-30.

statute.title: Effect of obtaining personal services income through a personal services entity
Deductions of personal services entity
Withholding obligations

nodes.label: Is the expense one an employee could deduct (s 85-10)?
nodes.body: s 85-10(1): no deduction for amounts relating to PSI that you could not deduct if you were an employee. s 85-10(2) preserves: (a) gaining work (advertising, tendering, quoting), (b) income/earning-capacity insurance, (c) liability insurance, (d) engaging a non-associate, (e) engaging an associate for principal work, (f) your own super, (g) workers' comp obligations, (h) other prescribed amounts.

statute.title: Deductions for non-employees relating to personal services income

nodes.label: Deductible (employee-equivalent or s 85-10(2) preserved)
nodes.body: Expenses an employee could deduct (work tools, professional development) are deductible; s 85-10(2) categories preserved. TR 2020/1 illustrates the employee baseline.

nodes.label: Not deductible under Div 85
nodes.body: Denied: not employee-deductible (s 85-10(1)), residence occupancy (s 85-15), associate payment outside s 85-20(2), or associate super outside s 85-25(2). Payments to associates denied are not income of the associate either (s 85-20(3)).

nodes.label: FACET — Results test (s 87-18): 75% threshold
nodes.body: Where to look: s 87-18; TR 2022/3. Pass if, for at least 75% of your PSI: (a) income is for producing a result, (b) you supply plant/equipment/tools of trade, (c) you are liable for rectifying defects. The 75% is of PSI received during the year. See s 87-18(1)-(4) for details and exceptions.

statute.title: The results test for a personal services business

rulings.title: personal services income and personal services businesses

nodes.label: FACET — Unrelated clients test (s 87-20): 2+ clients
nodes.body: Where to look: s 87-20; TR 2022/3. Pass if you obtained PSI from 2+ entities that are not associates of each other or of you, AND the PSI was not produced as a result of you being told what to do and how. Note: if 80% or more of PSI is from one source, the unrelated clients test (and employment/business premises tests) do not apply — only results test counts (s 87-15(3)).

statute.title: The unrelated clients test for a personal services business

rulings.title: personal services income and personal services businesses

nodes.label: FACET — Employment test (s 87-25)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 87-25; TR 2022/3. Pass if you engage entities (not associates who are individuals) to perform work, and the work is not PSI of the engaging entity, and the individuals performing the work are not employees of yours and do not receive PSI from you. Note: s 87-15(3) may restrict this test if 80%+ from one source.

statute.title: The employment test for a personal services business

rulings.title: personal services income and personal services businesses

nodes.label: FACET — Business premises test (s 87-30)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 87-30; TR 2022/3. Pass if you maintain business premises (NOT your or an associate's residence) at which you mainly perform the work, the premises are used mainly to produce the PSI, and they are physically separate from the acquirer's premises. Note: s 87-15(3) may restrict this test if 80%+ from one source.

statute.title: The business premises test for a personal services business

rulings.title: personal services income and personal services businesses

nodes.label: FACET — Entity deduction entitlements (s 86-60)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 86-60. A PSE cannot deduct an amount relating to an individual's PSI unless (a) the individual could have deducted it in the same circumstances (employee-equivalence, per Div 85 limits), or (b) the entity receives the PSI in conducting a PSB. Note: the 80% source-concentration rule (affecting which PSB tests can be used) is in s 87-15(3), not s 86-60.

statute.title: General rule for deduction entitlements of personal services entities

nodes.label: FACET — Associate super cap (s 85-25(3)): SG ceiling
nodes.body: Where to look: s 85-25. You can deduct super for an associate whose work forms part of the principal work (s 85-25(2)) — but the deduction is capped at the super guarantee amount you would have had to contribute for the associate (s 85-25(3)-(4)). The cap is calculated on the salary/wages not denied by ss 85-10/85-20.
